captions.instagram:
How does the pancreas work?

Behind your stomach sits a soft, 15 cm organ that does two jobs at once: it pours out a litre or more of digestive juice a day, and a million tiny islands inside it keep your blood sugar steady with insulin. Take it apart in 3D, watch a beta cell taste sugar, and see what goes wrong in diabetes.

→ Hidden behind your stomach is a soft, 15 cm organ: the pancreas.
→ It is two organs in one: a juice factory, dotted with a million islets that make hormones.
→ Grape-like clusters of cells pack digestive enzymes into tiny parcels, then release them into the ducts.
→ Trypsin leaves switched off. Only inside the gut is it switched on, so the pancreas never digests itself.
→ Sugar in, ATP up, potassium gates shut, calcium floods in, and insulin pours out.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/pancreasclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the pancreas work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Behind your stomach sits a soft, 15 cm organ that does two jobs at once: it pours out a litre or more of digestive juice a day, and a million tiny islands inside it keep your blood sugar steady with insulin. Take it apart in 3D, watch a beta cell taste sugar, and see what goes wrong in diabetes.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/pancreasclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/pancreasclear

In this video:
• Two organs in one. The pancreas lies behind the stomach, about 15 cm long and 80 g, with its head in the C of the duodenum and its tail at the spleen.
• A juice factory with a safety lock. Acinar cells make amylase, lipase and protein-cutting enzymes, about 1 to 1.5 litres of juice a day.
• A cell that tastes sugar. Beta cells burn glucose to make ATP.
• A thermostat for blood sugar. Insulin lets muscle and fat take in glucose and tells the liver to store it; glucagon tells the liver to release it.
• When the thermostat breaks. In type 1 diabetes the immune system destroys the beta cells.
• Keeping it healthy. Pancreatitis happens when enzymes switch on inside the gland, most often after gallstones or heavy alcohol use, and needs urgent care.
